source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Use a gait belt and perform a one-person transfer before determining whether the client can bear weight.","B":"Manually lift the client’s full body weight when the transfer distance is short and a second nurse is nearby.","C":"Assess the client’s mobility and assistance needs, then use appropriate assistive equipment and additional staff when indicated.","D":"Begin the transfer without equipment, then add a device only if the client becomes unstable while standing."}}
source_row.rationale: NIOSH identifies patient handling as a major musculoskeletal-injury risk and recommends safe patient-handling and mobility strategies, including appropriate assistive lifting devices. Transfer planning should be based on the patient's mobility and assistance needs rather than routine manual lifting.
source_row.source_detail: Safe patient handling includes use of assistive lifting technology and appropriate procedures to reduce injury risk during lifting, moving, and repositioning. Source has no separate formal version identifier in the cited page metadata; live currentness and applicability rechecked 2026-08-15. NCSBN first-check: Client Needs — Physiological Integrity — Basic Care and Comfort: mobility, assistive devices, hygiene, nutrition, elimination, comfort and nonpharmacological basic-care activities as applicable. 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan; effective 2026-04-01 through 2029-03-31; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.
